title: Project Management Tracker
spec: Implement `manage(events)`. The function must process a sequence of project event tuples. Track six separate project categories: open bugs, resolved bugs, planned features, finished features, active developers, and system logs. Depending on the event type contained in each tuple, route the associated data to the appropriate category. As you collect system logs, group them by their severity level, initializing a new grouping sequence for any previously unseen severity level. Extract the management of active developers into a helper routine that independently tracks front end developers and back end developers utilizing its own separate collections. Return a tuple containing the final counts or lengths of the six primary tracking categories. Example input: a sequence of project event tuples containing type, description, and metadata. Example output: a tuple of six integers representing the category sizes.

title: Fantasy Game Inventory
spec: Implement `equip(commands)`. Process a sequence of inventory command tuples for a player character. Keep tabs on six distinct storage areas: equipped weapons, equipped armor, healing potions, quest items, gold pouches, and discarded items. Each command specifies an action and an item to store or remove. Whenever an item is routed to discarded items, group it by its material type, forming a new category sequence the first time a new material is encountered. Utilize a secondary helper procedure to evaluate the healing potions, internally keeping separate records for minor potions and major potions using fresh local tracking structures. Return a tuple of six integers reflecting the total items or keys currently in each main storage area. Example input: a sequence of inventory command tuples. Example output: a tuple of six numeric totals.

title: Text Document Indexer
spec: Implement `index(paragraphs)`. Process a list of text paragraphs to build a document summary. Maintain separate collections for word frequencies, inverted positions, paragraph lengths, unique words per paragraph, skipped stop words, and punctuation counts. As you compile inverted positions, group the locations by the specific word, starting a new position sequence whenever a previously unrecorded word appears. Write a helper routine to process the skipped stop words, tracking short stop words and long stop words independently using its own local structures. The main routine should ultimately yield a tuple of numbers representing the total keys or elements in each of the six primary tracking collections. Example input: a sequence of paragraph strings. Example output: a tuple of six summary integers.

title: University Course Registration
spec: Implement `register(requests)`. Evaluate a sequence of student course registration tuples. Track enrolled students, waitlisted students, rejected requests, student credit totals, course capacities, and instructor assignments. When a student request is routed to rejected requests, group the rejections by the academic department, beginning a new sequence for any new department. Delegate the assignment of instructors to a distinct helper procedure that monitors morning classes and afternoon classes using its own localized tracking collections. Return a tuple of six numerical summaries representing the total entries in each primary tracking category. Example input: a sequence of student request tuples. Example output: a tuple of six summary integers.

title: Server Log Analyzer
spec: Implement `analyze(logs)`. Scan a sequence of web server log entries. You must track active sessions, timed out sessions, error endpoints, success endpoints, user agents, and hit counts. While parsing the error endpoints, group them by the specific HTTP status code, establishing a fresh grouping whenever a new status code appears. Create an auxiliary routine to parse the user agents, which internally tracks mobile browsers and desktop browsers separately before returning its results. The main routine should return a tuple of six integers indicating the size or length of the primary monitoring collections. Example input: a sequence of server log tuples. Example output: a tuple of six integer counts.

title: E-commerce Order Fulfillment
spec: Implement `fulfill(orders)`. Process incoming online order details. Keep tabs on packed items, backordered items, shipped boxes, cancelled orders, customer notifications, and refund lists. Whenever an item is designated as backordered, group it by the supplier name, forming a new sequence for each new supplier encountered. Implement a helper procedure to process the cancelled orders, which needs to independently track fraudulent cancellations and user requested cancellations using its own fresh collections. Return a tuple of six integers that capture the final tally of each major order category. Example input: a sequence of order tuples. Example output: a tuple of six numeric tallies.

title: Social Media Network Analyzer
spec: Implement `analyze(connections)`. Evaluate user connection events on a social platform. Track followers, following lists, mutual friends, blocked users, muted users, and pending requests. When handling blocked users, group the blocks by the reported reason, setting up a new grouping for any newly encountered reason. Utilize a secondary helper routine to evaluate the pending requests, internally keeping separate records for requests older than a week and recent requests. Conclude by returning a tuple of six sizes corresponding to the main tracking collections. Example input: a sequence of connection action tuples. Example output: a tuple of six collection sizes.

title: Smart Home Device Controller
spec: Implement `automate(triggers)`. Process a timeline of smart home sensor triggers. Track active lights, unlocked doors, triggered alarms, silent routines, scheduled events, and offline devices. While managing triggered alarms, categorize them by the home zone, initiating a new category sequence the first time a zone reports an alarm. Build an auxiliary procedure to handle the scheduled events, maintaining independent groupings for morning routines and evening routines with localized structures. Return a tuple containing the final count of elements within each of the six primary tracking structures. Example input: a sequence of sensor trigger tuples. Example output: a six element tuple of counts.

title: Restaurant Kitchen Ticket System
spec: Implement `kitchen(tickets)`. Handle a stream of food order tickets for a busy restaurant. You are required to track appetizers, main courses, desserts, drink orders, voided items, and completed plates. As voided items are processed, organize them by the server who placed the order, creating a new grouping whenever a new server voids an item. Route the drink orders through a specialized helper routine that independently tallies alcoholic beverages and non alcoholic beverages using localized collections. Return a tuple of six integers reflecting the total items or keys in each main tracking group. Example input: a sequence of order item tuples. Example output: a tuple of six integer counts.

title: Library Book Circulation
spec: Implement `circulate(transactions)`. Process a daily log of library book actions. Monitor available books, checked out books, overdue fines, reserved titles, lost books, and damaged copies. When tracking damaged copies, group them by the condition rating, initializing a new sequence for any new condition rating encountered. Use a helper function to calculate the overdue fines, which must separately keep track of adult fines and children fines using its own isolated collections. Return a six element tuple containing the numerical size of each primary monitoring collection. Example input: a sequence of library action tuples. Example output: a six element integer tuple.

title: Online Chat Room Moderator
spec: Implement `moderate(messages)`. Evaluate a continuous stream of chat room messages. Track active chatters, warned users, banned accounts, flagged words, deleted messages, and pinned announcements. While tracking flagged words, categorize them by their severity level, starting a new category whenever an unseen severity is detected. Delegate the processing of deleted messages to a secondary helper routine that maintains separate tallies for automated deletions and manual deletions. Finally, return a tuple of six integers representing the final sizes of the main collections. Example input: a sequence of chat message tuples. Example output: a tuple of six counts.

title: Flight Traffic Control Simulator
spec: Implement `route(flights)`. Manage a list of air traffic control events. You must track grounded planes, airborne planes, landing queues, takeoff queues, delayed flights, and canceled routes. For delayed flights, group them by their destination airport, forming a new grouping the first time a destination experiences a delay. Formulate a separate helper procedure to manage the canceled routes, keeping independent track of weather cancellations and mechanical cancellations using fresh collections. Return a tuple of six numbers denoting the total entries in each primary tracking section. Example input: a sequence of flight event tuples. Example output: a tuple of six numeric totals.

title: Personal Finance Budgeter
spec: Implement `budget(transactions)`. Analyze a sequence of personal financial transactions. Keep records of housing expenses, food costs, entertainment spending, savings deposits, debt payments, and unmapped transactions. When recording entertainment spending, group the transactions by the vendor name, creating a new transaction sequence for each new vendor. Implement a helper routine to review the unmapped transactions, establishing separate tracking for recurring mysteries and one time mysteries. Return a tuple composed of six integers that summarize the volume of each main transaction category. Example input: a sequence of transaction tuples. Example output: a tuple of six summary integers.

title: Music Playlist Generator
spec: Implement `curate(tracks)`. Process a list of user listening history events to build new playlists. Track upbeat songs, chill songs, workout tracks, blocked artists, favorite genres, and recently played songs. As you categorize blocked artists, group them by the reason for blocking, instantiating a new group for any newly cited reason. Create a helper routine to analyze the recently played songs, internally separating them into instrumental tracks and vocal tracks using localized tracking collections. Output a tuple of six integers reflecting the item counts in each primary category. Example input: a sequence of song history tuples. Example output: a tuple of six numbers.

title: Weather Station Data Aggregator
spec: Implement `aggregate(readings)`. Compile environmental sensor readings from a weather station. Maintain records for daily highs, daily lows, precipitation amounts, wind gusts, error readings, and battery warnings. When tracking error readings, organize them by the specific sensor module, starting a new sequence for each distinct module that fails. Rely on a separate helper procedure to evaluate the precipitation amounts, keeping independent tracking for rain events and snow events. Return a six value tuple representing the total elements aggregated in each main category. Example input: a sequence of weather reading tuples. Example output: a six element tuple of totals.

title: Voting System Tabulator
spec: Implement `tabulate(ballots)`. Process a batch of election ballots. Track valid votes, spoiled ballots, absentee submissions, late arrivals, challenged signatures, and write in candidates. For spoiled ballots, group them by the specific precinct number, establishing a fresh grouping for any new precinct. Extract the handling of write in candidates into a helper routine that independently organizes serious candidates and joke candidates utilizing its own fresh collections. Return a tuple of six integers showing the total ballots or categories within the primary tracking structures. Example input: a sequence of ballot tuples. Example output: a tuple of six integers.

title: Hotel Reservation Manager
spec: Implement `book(requests)`. Manage a daily ledger of guest accommodation requests. Track available rooms, available suites, occupied rooms, maintenance queues, early check ins, and late check outs. As maintenance queues are recorded, categorize them by the required repair type, creating a new category whenever a new repair type is logged. Utilize a helper procedure to process the early check ins, maintaining separate records for loyalty members and standard guests. Yield a tuple of six counts representing the final capacities of the main tracking ledgers. Example input: a sequence of accommodation request tuples. Example output: a tuple of six numeric capacities.

title: Fleet Vehicle Dispatcher
spec: Implement `dispatch(vehicles)`. Monitor the status of a regional delivery fleet. Keep tracking for idle trucks, active trucks, repair queues, driver assignments, route manifests, and delayed shipments. When updating delayed shipments, group them by the transit region, starting a new sequence for each newly affected region. Design a separate helper procedure to organize repair queues, which internally segregates routine maintenance and critical breakdowns using distinct localized collections. The main entry point should return a tuple of six integers indicating the size of each primary tracking pool. Example input: a sequence of fleet update tuples. Example output: a tuple of six summary figures.

title: Recipe Ingredient Parser
spec: Implement `parse(recipes)`. Analyze a collection of culinary recipe submissions. Track dry ingredients, wet ingredients, spices, allergens, substitution options, and missing items. While logging allergens, group them by the severity of the reaction, initiating a new grouping for any previously unrecorded severity. Construct a helper routine to handle the substitution options, keeping independent records for vegan substitutes and gluten free substitutes. Conclude by returning a tuple of six numbers corresponding to the number of items or keys in each main tracking category. Example input: a sequence of ingredient data tuples. Example output: a tuple of six counts.

title: Customer Support Ticketing
spec: Implement `support(tickets)`. Handle a queue of incoming customer service queries. Track unassigned tickets, escalated issues, resolved queries, pending replies, spam messages, and priority alerts. When classifying priority alerts, group them by the affected product line, creating a new grouping sequence for each new product line encountered. Use a helper routine to sift through the spam messages, organizing them independently into promotional spam and malicious attempts. Return a six element tuple detailing the total volume in each primary ticketing category. Example input: a sequence of customer query tuples. Example output: a six element tuple of totals.

title: Blockchain Transaction Pool
spec: Implement `verify(blocks)`. Process a stream of decentralized network transactions. Track pending transactions, confirmed transactions, orphaned blocks, invalid signatures, high fee items, and network peers. When handling orphaned blocks, group them by the miner address, beginning a new sequence for each distinct miner. Develop a helper function to inspect the invalid signatures, maintaining separate internal tracking for expired timestamps and malformed keys. Return a tuple of six integer counts representing the load in each of the main transaction trackers. Example input: a sequence of network block tuples. Example output: a tuple of six transaction counts.

title: Wildlife Tracking Grid
spec: Implement `monitor(sightings)`. Analyze telemetry data from a nature preserve. Track predator locations, prey herds, migratory birds, injured animals, stationary cameras, and weather alerts. As you log injured animals, categorize them by the species name, forming a new category the first time a new species is reported. Route the weather alerts through a helper routine that independently monitors severe storms and mild warnings using distinct tracking collections. The primary routine must return a tuple of six numbers showing the total elements in each primary tracking dataset. Example input: a sequence of wildlife observation tuples. Example output: a tuple of six dataset totals.

title: Fitness App Workout Logger
spec: Implement `log(exercises)`. Evaluate a week of user fitness activity logs. Maintain records for cardio sessions, weight lifting sets, stretching routines, skipped days, personal records, and caloric estimates. When logging personal records, group them by the specific exercise name, establishing a new grouping sequence for any newly mastered exercise. Build a helper procedure to process the stretching routines, isolating dynamic stretches and static stretches into separate localized tracking variables. Return a tuple of six numeric counts summarizing the main fitness tracking categories. Example input: a sequence of workout event tuples. Example output: a tuple of six numeric counts.

title: Assembly Line Quality Control
spec: Implement `inspect(widgets)`. Process a batch of factory production line reports. Keep track of passed items, minor defects, critical failures, rework queues, scrapped parts, and inspector notes. When sorting critical failures, group them by the responsible machine identifier, starting a new failure sequence for each newly identified machine. Utilize a helper routine to manage the inspector notes, keeping independent track of positive feedback and safety warnings using its own fresh tracking variables. Output a tuple of six integers representing the final count of items in each primary production category. Example input: a sequence of factory report tuples. Example output: a tuple of six item counts.

title: Real Estate Property Manager
spec: Implement `manage(properties)`. Review a portfolio of property management updates. Track vacant units, occupied apartments, pending leases, eviction notices, maintenance requests, and tenant complaints. As you log maintenance requests, categorize them by the building zone, opening a new grouping for any zone reporting an issue for the first time. Delegate the review of tenant complaints to an auxiliary helper function that internally tracks noise complaints and cleanliness complaints using distinct tracking collections. Return a tuple of six summary integers detailing the volume in each primary management category. Example input: a sequence of property update tuples. Example output: a tuple of six volume integers.

title: Transport Network Pathfinder
spec: Write a function explore(connections) that processes a sequence of transport links between cities. Each link is a tuple of two cities and a distance. The algorithm must group the links by origin city into a mapping. It must also initialize a queue of cities to explore, a list of visited cities, a mapping of shortest known distances from the starting city, and a mapping of predecessors to reconstruct paths. Additionally, it should track dead ends in a collection, alternative routes in another collection, and a sequence of explored nodes. The function should compute shortest paths from the first city to all others, returning a tuple containing the explored sequence and the dead ends. Example input: a link from alpha to beta with distance ten. Output: a tuple with the explored cities and any dead ends.

title: Code Bracket Validator
spec: Write a function parse(tokens) that evaluates a sequence of text tokens representing source code. The function must maintain a stack for open parentheses, a stack for open brackets, and a stack for open braces. It also needs to collect syntax errors, unmatched symbols, and valid code blocks in separate sequences. Furthermore, it must track the line numbers of each open block using a mapping, and keep a mapping of variable names defined within the current scope. Processing the tokens one by one, it should match closing brackets with their respective open ones, recording an error if they mismatch. It returns a tuple containing the valid blocks, errors, and unmatched symbols. Example input: open brace, identifier, close brace. Output: one block, zero errors, and zero unmatched symbols.

title: Medical Supply Router
spec: Write a function route(shipments) that distributes medical packages across a hospital network. The input is a sequence of tuples containing package identifier, destination department, and urgency level. The function must initialize separate lists for critical priority packages, standard priority packages, delayed packages, and refrigerated items. It also needs a mapping for courier assignments, a mapping for storage hubs, a sequence of failed deliveries, and a mapping of dispatch times. For each shipment, it evaluates the urgency and destination, assigning it to a courier if capacity allows, or placing it in the delayed list. The function returns a tuple of the critical priority list, the standard list, and failed deliveries. Example input: package one to surgery with critical priority. Output: tuple where the first element contains package one, and the others are empty sequences.

title: Tournament Pairing Engine
spec: Write a function pair(players) that organizes the first round of a competition. The input is a sequence of participant names. The engine must maintain lists for active players, eliminated players, disqualified players, and players receiving a bye. It also needs mappings to track individual scores, historical opponents to avoid rematches, assigned color preferences, and tiebreaker points. The function must pair active players sequentially, storing the matchups in another list, and if the number of players is odd, select one for the bye list. It should return a tuple of the matchups and the bye player. Example input: sequence of three names. Output: one matchup tuple and one bye.

title: Message Spam Classifier
spec: Write a function classify(messages) that evaluates text messages for unwanted content. The input is a sequence of strings. The classifier must build a list of suspicious words, a list of clean words, a list of unknown terms, and a list of internal links encountered during processing. It must also maintain mappings for the frequency of suspicious words per sender, the reputation score of each domain, a mapping of flagged attachments, and a quarantine area for flagged messages. Each message is split into words and evaluated against built-in rules, updating the frequencies and routing the message. It returns a tuple of the clean messages and the quarantined messages. Example input: one clean message and one containing lottery. Output: one clean and one quarantined.

title: Operating System Memory Allocator
spec: Write a function allocate(requests) that simulates a memory management unit. The input is a sequence of integers representing memory block sizes requested by processes. The simulation must track free memory blocks, allocated memory blocks, fragmented blocks, and reserved system blocks using separate lists. It also requires mappings to associate process identifiers with their allocated blocks, a registry of out of memory errors, a mapping of deallocation events, and a list of waiting processes. As each request is processed, it either takes a block from the free blocks or adds the process to the waiting list. The function returns a tuple of the allocated blocks and the waiting processes. Example input: requests for ten and twenty units. Output: allocated blocks for both if space permits, else one waits.

title: Intersection Traffic Simulator
spec: Write a function direct(vehicles) that processes cars arriving at a four way intersection. The input is a sequence of tuples detailing arrival time, direction of approach, and intended turn. The simulator must maintain separate waiting lists for northbound, southbound, eastbound, and westbound traffic. It also needs a mapping to track the signal state for each direction, a list of vehicles that have cleared the intersection, a mapping of wait times per vehicle, and a list of emergency vehicles. The logic evaluates arrival times to move vehicles from the waiting lists to the cleared list. It returns a list of cleared vehicles in chronological order. Example input: a vehicle arriving north at time zero. Output: a list containing that vehicle clearing at time one.

title: Source Code Tokenizer
spec: Write a function tokenize(characters) that converts a raw string of code into meaningful symbols. The analyzer must group characters into distinct lists for keywords, identifiers, numeric literals, operators, and punctuation marks. It must also maintain a mapping of recognized variables, a mapping of constant values, a list for lexical errors such as invalid characters, and a list of comments to be ignored. By iterating over the characters, it identifies word boundaries and categorizes each segment, updating the respective lists and mappings. The function returns a tuple of the identifiers, literals, and errors. Example input: a string assigning five to a variable. Output: the variable name in identifiers, five in literals, and no errors.

title: Relational Data Joiner
spec: Write a function combine(tables) that merges two datasets based on a common key. The input is a tuple of two sequences representing the left and right tables, where each row is a tuple of key and value. The engine must build a mapping for the left table index, a mapping for the right table index, a list for successfully matched rows, a list for left rows with no match, a list for right rows with no match, a list for duplicate keys, a mapping for merge conflicts, and a list of filtered invalid rows. The function populates the indexes and iterates through them to find intersections, appending results to the match or mismatch lists. It returns a tuple of matches, left orphans, and right orphans. Example input: left table with key one, right table with key one. Output: one match, no orphans.

title: Dependency Task Scheduler
spec: Write a function schedule(jobs) that determines the execution order of interdependent processes. The input is a sequence of tuples representing a job and its prerequisite. The scheduler must construct a mapping for the adjacency graph of dependencies, a mapping of incoming edge counts for each job, a list of ready jobs, a list of completed jobs, a list of failed jobs, a list of delayed jobs, a list of circular dependencies, and a mapping for execution logs. By processing the ready list and decrementing the edge counts of dependent jobs, it builds the completion sequence. It returns a tuple of the completed jobs and any jobs caught in a circular dependency. Example input: job two depends on job one. Output: job one then job two in the completed sequence.

title: Bowling Game Scorer
spec: Write a function score(rolls) that calculates the points in a bowling match. The input is a sequence of pins knocked down per roll. The scorer must maintain a list of regular frames, a list of strike frames, a list of spare frames, and a list of open frames. It also needs a mapping of player totals, a mapping of active bonuses, a list of fouls, and a list of split conversions. The logic iterates through the rolls to group them into frames, determining if each is a strike, spare, or open, and applies bonus points to previous frames accordingly. The function returns a tuple of the final score and the strike frames. Example input: sequence of twenty zeros. Output: zero score and no strikes.

title: Network Protocol Router
spec: Write a function route(packets) that simulates a distance vector routing protocol. The input is a sequence of network messages. The simulation must initialize a mapping for the local routing table, a mapping for neighbor states, a list of routing updates, a list of link state changes, a list of dropped packets, a list of forwarded packets, a mapping of packet latencies, and a list of unreachable destinations. As messages arrive, the routing table is updated and packets are placed in the forwarded or dropped lists based on the known neighbors. The function returns a tuple of the forwarded packets and the dropped packets. Example input: message to a known neighbor. Output: one forwarded packet, zero dropped.

title: Gene Sequence Alignment
spec: Write a function align(sequences) that compares multiple biological strings. The input is a sequence of character strings representing genetic data. The algorithm must track a list of exact matches, a list of partial mismatches, a list of introduced gaps, and a list of unaligned regions. It also requires a mapping of alignment scores, a mapping of mutation frequencies, a list of consensus sequences, and a mapping of sequence lengths. By iterating through the strings and comparing characters at each position, it builds the alignments and updates the scores. The function returns a tuple of the exact matches and the unaligned regions. Example input: two identical strings. Output: full exact match and zero unaligned regions.

title: Cinema Seating Optimizer
spec: Write a function seat(requests) that assigns tickets in a movie theater. The input is a sequence of party sizes requested by customers. The optimizer must maintain a list of booked seats, a list of available seats, a list of aisle seats, and a list of rejected groups due to lack of space. It also needs a mapping of party identities to their assigned rows, a mapping of VIP reservations, a list of split groups, and a list of refunded tickets. The logic processes each request, attempting to find contiguous available seats before splitting a group or rejecting them. The function returns a tuple of the booked seats and the rejected groups. Example input: request for two seats in an empty theater. Output: two booked seats, zero rejected.

title: Mark and Sweep Collector
spec: Write a function collect(memory) that simulates a garbage collection cycle. The input is a sequence of object references and their current linkages. The simulator must maintain a list of root objects, a list of marked objects, a list of swept objects, and a list of free memory blocks. It also needs a mapping of object sizes, a mapping of reference counts, a list of circular references, and a list of pinned objects that cannot be moved. The cycle begins by traversing from the root objects to populate the marked list, then iterates over all memory to place unmarked items into the swept and free lists. The function returns a tuple of the freed blocks and the marked objects. Example input: one root pointing to one object. Output: zero freed blocks, two marked objects.

title: Vending Machine Inventory
spec: Write a function vend(transactions) that manages the stock and currency of an automated dispenser. The input is a sequence of purchase attempts containing item selection and inserted coins. The machine must track a list of dispensed items, a list of returned coins, a list of out of stock errors, and a list of insufficient funds errors. It must also maintain a mapping of current inventory counts, a mapping of item prices, a mapping of collected currency denominations, and a list of maintenance alerts. For each transaction, it verifies stock and payment, updating inventory and coin collections or issuing errors. The function returns a tuple of the dispensed items and returned coins. Example input: sufficient coins for a stocked item. Output: one dispensed item and any change in returned coins.

title: Elevator Control Logic
spec: Write a function transport(calls) that dictates the movement of a building elevator. The input is a sequence of floor requests from passengers. The controller must maintain a list of requests to go up, a list of requests to go down, a list of boarded passengers, and a list of dropped off passengers. It also requires a mapping of floor access permissions, a mapping of waiting times, a list of skipped floors, and a list of idle states. The logic processes the calls to determine the elevator direction, stopping at requested floors to board or drop off passengers based on the current direction. The function returns a tuple of dropped off passengers and the skipped floors. Example input: call from floor two to floor five. Output: passenger dropped off at five, and zero skipped floors.

title: Card Game Dealer
spec: Write a function deal(actions) that simulates a round of a tabletop card game. The input is a sequence of player moves and wagers. The dealer must maintain a list of cards in the deck, a list of cards in the discard pile, a list of cards on the table, and a list of eliminated players. It also needs a mapping of cards in each player hand, a mapping of current bets per player, a mapping of total chip counts, and a list of invalid moves. The simulation shuffles the deck, distributes cards to the hands, and processes the actions to update bets and chip counts. The function returns a tuple of the table cards and the eliminated players. Example input: two players betting ten chips each. Output: empty table cards and zero eliminated players.

title: Supermarket Checkout Queue
spec: Write a function checkout(shoppers) that manages customer flow at a retail store. The input is a sequence of customer carts, each containing items to purchase. The manager must track a list of scanned items, a list of bagged items, a list of applied coupons, and a list of voided transactions. It must also maintain a mapping of cashier stations to their current customer, a mapping of receipt totals, a list of price check delays, and a list of loyalty card members. Customers are routed to available cashiers, where items are moved to the scanned and bagged lists. The function returns a tuple of the scanned items and the voided transactions. Example input: one customer with one item. Output: one scanned item, zero voided.

title: File System Directory Builder
spec: Write a function build(paths) that constructs a virtual file system tree from a list of flat paths. The input is a sequence of file path strings. The builder must maintain a list of root directories, a list of nested subdirectories, a list of regular files, and a list of symbolic links. It also requires a mapping of file sizes, a mapping of access permissions, a mapping of file extension types, and a list of path parsing errors. As each path is split by its separator, the components are categorized into the respective lists and mappings are initialized for the files. The function returns a tuple of the root directories and the parsing errors. Example input: sequence containing one simple file path. Output: one regular file, zero errors.

title: Spell Checker Engine
spec: Write a function check(words) that provides corrections for misspelled text. The input is a sequence of text strings. The engine must track a list of correct words, a list of misspelled words, a list of ignored punctuation, and a list of numerical digits. It also needs a mapping of suggested corrections for each error, a mapping of known prefixes, a mapping of known suffixes, and a list of custom dictionary additions. By comparing each word against a simple rule set, it separates them into correct or misspelled lists and generates candidates for the mapping of suggestions. The function returns a tuple of the misspelled words and the ignored punctuation. Example input: sequence with one known word and one typo. Output: one misspelled word and zero ignored punctuation.

title: Railway Conflict Detector
spec: Write a function dispatch(trains) that monitors a railway network for potential collisions. The input is a sequence of train routes, each detailing departure time and track segments. The detector must maintain a list of active trains, a list of delayed trains, a list of rerouted trains, and a list of arrived trains. It also requires a mapping of track segment occupancies, a mapping of station arrival times, a list of detected conflicts, and a list of emergency stops. The simulation advances time, moving trains along segments and recording a conflict if two trains require the same segment simultaneously. The function returns a tuple of the detected conflicts and the arrived trains. Example input: two trains scheduled on the same track at the same time. Output: one detected conflict, zero arrived.

title: Factory Material Costing
spec: Write a function cost(products) that calculates the profit margins for manufactured goods. The input is a sequence of items, where each item is a tuple of name, required parts, and selling price. The calculator must maintain a list of high margin goods, a list of loss leaders, a list of eco friendly options, and a list of export only items. It also needs a mapping of component unit costs, a mapping of assembly times, a list of out of stock parts, and a mapping of supplier contacts. By iterating through the products and summing the component costs from the mapping, it categorizes each good based on its profitability. The function returns a tuple of the high margin goods and the out of stock parts. Example input: one product with cheap parts and high price. Output: product in high margin list, zero missing parts.

title: Subscription Billing Processor
spec: Write a function bill(accounts) that manages recurring payments for a software service. The input is a sequence of user subscription records. The processor must maintain a list of active subscriptions, a list of suspended accounts, a list of expired trials, and a list of canceled memberships. It also requires a mapping of successful payment amounts, a mapping of failed transaction reasons, a list of generated invoices, and a mapping of promotional discounts applied. Each account is evaluated for its renewal date and payment status, routing it to the appropriate list and updating the mappings. The function returns a tuple of the generated invoices and the suspended accounts. Example input: one account with a valid payment. Output: one generated invoice, zero suspended.

title: Cloud Resource Load Balancer
spec: Write a function balance(requests) that distributes web traffic across multiple servers. The input is a sequence of incoming client connections. The balancer must maintain a list of active connections, a list of pending requests, a list of dropped requests, and a list of completed sessions. It also needs a mapping of server capacities, a mapping of current server loads, a list of offline servers, and a mapping of client ip addresses to assigned servers. As requests arrive, they are routed to the server with the lowest load in the mapping, or added to the dropped list if all servers are at capacity. The function returns a tuple of the active connections and the dropped requests. Example input: one request with available servers. Output: one active connection, zero dropped.

title: Distribution Center Sorter
spec: The entry function is sort(packages) which groups bulk shipment records into processing zones. The algorithm must maintain individual lists for hazardous materials, fragile items, heavy cargo, and standard goods. It needs to establish a registry mapping tracking numbers to their final destinations and a separate directory linking processing zones to driver names. Maintain a queue for items requiring manual inspection and a list for entirely rejected parcels. Return a tuple containing the total count of valid packages and the number of rejected packages. For example, given a batch of thirty varied items, it might return twenty-eight and two.

title: Taxonomy Tree Builder
spec: The entry function build(organisms) processes flat species records to form a biological hierarchy. Initialize a mapping for the root domains, a tracking directory for known kingdoms, and a separate registry for phyla. Maintain distinct lists to collect newly discovered species, extinct species, and unclassified genetic anomalies. Keep a registry mapping scientific names to their common names and a separate mapping for habitat types. Return a tuple with the total categorized species and the count of unclassified anomalies.

title: Multiplayer Matchmaker System
spec: The entry function match(players) organizes connected users into game lobbies based on skill level. Initialize separate queues for novice, intermediate, advanced, and expert players. Create a mapping of player identifiers to their latency scores and a registry linking formed teams to their selected characters. Keep lists for players waiting for teammates, disconnected users, and penalized users. Return a tuple of total active matches and total players currently waiting.

title: Telecom Call Router
spec: The entry function route(calls) processes incoming customer service requests. Maintain distinct waiting queues for billing issues, technical support, sales inquiries, and account cancellations. Initialize a directory of available agents and a mapping of currently active conversations. Track escalated calls in a specialized list and dropped calls in another separate list. Return a tuple showing the number of connected calls and the number of waiting calls. For example, an input of fifty calls might result in thirty connected and twenty waiting.

title: Factory Assembly Coordinator
spec: The entry function coordinate(parts) manages components flowing through a manufacturing line. Create separate buffers for raw materials, partially assembled units, finished goods, and defective components. Initialize a mapping for machine operational statuses and a registry of maintenance alerts. Keep a list for parts requiring manual inspection and a queue for recycling scraps. Return a tuple with the count of finished goods and the count of defective items.

title: Distance Learning Grader
spec: The entry function grade(submissions) evaluates student test answers and assigns them to performance brackets. Initialize a roster mapping student identifiers to their total scores and a registry mapping questions to their historical difficulty levels. Maintain separate lists for perfect scores, passing grades, failing grades, and flagged submissions requiring manual teacher review. Keep a registry of common mistakes and a mapping of overall topic mastery. Return a tuple with the class average score and the number of perfect scores.

title: Emergency Room Triage

Initialize a directory of available beds and a mapping of assigned attending doctors. Keep lists for patients needing immediate blood tests, patients waiting for imaging, and patients ready for discharge. Return a tuple containing the total admitted count and the discharged count.

title: Portfolio Asset Rebalancer

Create separate lists to track buy orders, sell orders, hold recommendations, and restricted insider trades. Maintain a queue for transactions pending broker approval and a list of failed transactions due to insufficient funds. Return a tuple of total executed trades and total failed trades.

title: Email Campaign Simulator
spec: A digital marketing system processes a sequence of message batches. The entry function is `campaign(batches)`. The system maintains six overall trackers, all initially empty: a dictionary of user email balances, a list of successfully delivered messages, a dictionary of bounce counts per address, a list of unsubscribed users, a dictionary of campaign open rates, and a list of delayed messages. The input is a list of batches, where each batch is a tuple containing a batch string and a sequence of individual action strings. For each batch, the logic must first create a temporary list of failed deliveries and a temporary dictionary of successful opens. It evaluates the actions: if an action is a success, it updates the temporary dictionary; if a failure, it appends to the temporary list. Afterwards, it merges these temporary items into the overall trackers by adding failures to the delayed messages list and updating the bounce counts. The function returns a tuple of the six overall trackers in the order described. For example, an empty input yields a tuple of six empty collections.

title: Retail Supply Chain
spec: A distribution center processes incoming shipment records. The entry function is `supply(shipments)`. It must initialize six overall trackers, all empty at the start: a dictionary of warehouse inventory, a list of completed deliveries, a dictionary of store shortages, a list of returned items, a dictionary of supplier payments, and a list of transit delays. The input comprises a list of shipment groups. Each group is a tuple with a region identifier and a sequence of transaction strings. For every group, the system creates a fresh list of damaged goods and a fresh dictionary of regional adjustments. It processes each transaction string, categorizing it to populate the fresh list and dictionary. Once the group is processed, the system merges the regional adjustments into the warehouse inventory dictionary and appends the damaged goods to the returned items list. Finally, it returns a tuple containing the six overall trackers. For instance, providing no shipments returns a tuple with six empty structures.

title: Online Auction Platform
spec: An internet bidding platform evaluates bidding sessions. The main function is `auction(sessions)`. It begins by establishing six empty global trackers: a dictionary of active item bids, a list of sold items, a dictionary of bidder balances, a list of suspended accounts, a dictionary of reserve prices, and a list of canceled bids. The input is a list of sessions, where each session is a tuple containing a session identifier and a sequence of bid amounts. During each session, the function must instantiate a local list of flagged bids and a local dictionary of session winners. As it iterates through the bid amounts, exceptionally high bids are added to the flagged list, while valid bids update the session winners dictionary. After processing the session, the flagged bids are transferred to the canceled bids list, and winners update the active item bids dictionary. The function ultimately returns a tuple of the six global trackers. Example: an input with zero sessions produces a tuple of six empty containers.

title: Hospital Bed Allocator
spec: A medical facility coordinates ward allocations across different shifts. The primary function is `hospital(shifts)`. It sets up six initially empty state containers: a dictionary of available beds, a list of discharged patients, a dictionary of ward capacities, a list of waitlisted patients, a dictionary of staff assignments, and a list of emergency transfers. The input consists of a list of shifts, each formatted as a tuple with a shift time and a sequence of admission requests. For each shift, the logic must generate a new list of critical alerts and a new dictionary of temporary rooms. It processes the admission requests to populate the alerts list for severe cases and the rooms dictionary for standard cases. Following the shift processing, critical alerts are appended to the emergency transfers list and the rooms dictionary updates the available beds dictionary. The function returns a tuple of the six state containers. For example, passing an empty list of shifts results in a tuple of six empty collections.

title: Freight Train Assembler
spec: A railway yard organizes departures based on daily schedules. The function to implement is `freight(schedules)`. It must define six empty tracking variables at the start: a dictionary of yard capacities, a list of dispatched trains, a dictionary of destination requirements, a list of maintenance cars, a dictionary of cargo weights, and a list of delayed departures. The input schedules are provided as a list of daily plans, each a tuple of a date and a sequence of cargo codes. For every daily plan, the system initializes a temporary list of hazardous materials and a temporary dictionary of track assignments. It inspects each cargo code, routing dangerous cargo to the hazardous list and standard cargo to the track assignments dictionary. At the end of the day, the hazardous materials are added to the maintenance cars list and the track assignments update the yard capacities dictionary. The function returns a tuple containing the six tracking variables. An empty schedules list will yield six empty collections as output.

title: Digital Newspaper Publisher
spec: A media outlet processes editorial content across multiple editions. The core function is `newspaper(editions)`. It requires six empty overall records: a dictionary of author royalties, a list of published articles, a dictionary of section word counts, a list of rejected drafts, a dictionary of editor workloads, and a list of trending topics. The input is a list of publishing editions, each represented by a tuple of an edition name and a sequence of article subjects. While processing each edition, the system must create a fresh list of breaking news and a fresh dictionary of keyword frequencies. The article subjects are analyzed to append urgent topics to the breaking news list and count terms in the keyword frequencies dictionary. After the edition, the breaking news is merged into the trending topics list and the keyword dictionary updates the section word counts dictionary. The function returns a tuple of the six overall records. For instance, an input of zero editions returns a tuple of six empty objects.

title: Pizzeria Order Tracker
spec: A restaurant tracks kitchen operations over several shifts. The main function is `pizzeria(shifts)`. It starts by creating six empty global containers: a dictionary of ingredient inventory, a list of completed orders, a dictionary of driver tips, a list of voided tickets, a dictionary of oven temperatures, and a list of pending deliveries. The shifts input is a list of periods, each a tuple of a period name and a sequence of order details. For every period, the logic must allocate a temporary list of allergy warnings and a temporary dictionary of special requests. It scans the order details, placing sensitive orders into the allergy list and customizations into the requests dictionary. At the end of the period, the allergy warnings are appended to the voided tickets list if they cannot be fulfilled, and the requests dictionary updates the ingredient inventory dictionary. The function returns a tuple of the six global containers. Passing an empty list produces a tuple of six empty trackers.

title: Solar Farm Monitor
spec: An energy company evaluates power generation across various days. The function `solar(days)` processes the data. It initializes six empty structures: a dictionary of panel outputs, a list of offline arrays, a dictionary of grid contributions, a list of maintenance requests, a dictionary of battery temperatures, and a list of grid faults. The input days are a list of daily logs, each a tuple of a date string and a sequence of power readings. During each daily log, the system formulates a new list of peak surges and a new dictionary of localized shading. Power readings are checked to add unusually high values to the surges list and low values to the shading dictionary. Once the day is evaluated, the peak surges are added to the grid faults list and the shading dictionary alters the panel outputs dictionary. The function concludes by returning a tuple of the six structures. For example, an empty input list yields a tuple of six empty elements.

title: Insurance Claim Processor
spec: An underwriter reviews claim submissions in billing cycles. The entry function is `insurance(cycles)`. It defines six empty master trackers: a dictionary of policy deductibles, a list of approved claims, a dictionary of adjuster workloads, a list of rejected applications, a dictionary of client premiums, and a list of pending reviews. The input consists of a list of cycles, each a tuple of a cycle identifier and a sequence of claim amounts. For each cycle, the logic establishes a local list of fraudulent flags and a local dictionary of coverage adjustments. Claim amounts are processed so that suspicious figures go to the flags list and normal figures update the adjustments dictionary. After reviewing the cycle, the flags are appended to the rejected applications list and the adjustments dictionary modifies the client premiums dictionary. The function returns a tuple of the six master trackers. Providing no cycles results in an output tuple of six empty structures.

title: Movie Theater Manager
spec: A cinema coordinates showings over multiple weekends. The required function is `theater(weekends)`. It begins with six empty primary trackers: a dictionary of screen capacities, a list of sold tickets, a dictionary of concession revenues, a list of refunded purchases, a dictionary of member points, and a list of upcoming premieres. The weekends input is a list of blocks, each a tuple of a weekend date and a sequence of patron requests. For every block, the system creates a temporary list of upgrade requests and a temporary dictionary of seat allocations. Patron requests are sorted, adding premium choices to the upgrade list and standard choices to the seat dictionary. At the block end, the upgrades are added to the sold tickets list and the seat dictionary updates the screen capacities dictionary. The function outputs a tuple of the six primary trackers. An empty list of weekends will return a tuple of six empty collections.

title: Symphony Orchestra Scheduler
spec: A musical director plans arrangements across different seasons. The processing function is `orchestra(seasons)`. It initializes six empty global records: a dictionary of musician salaries, a list of finalized performances, a dictionary of instrument repairs, a list of absent players, a dictionary of venue fees, and a list of special rehearsals. The input is a list of seasons, each a tuple of a season name and a sequence of availability codes. For each season, the logic must instantiate a fresh list of guest soloists and a fresh dictionary of piece durations. The availability codes dictate whether a performer is added to the guest list or used to update the durations dictionary. Afterward, the guest list is merged into the finalized performances list and the durations dictionary updates the venue fees dictionary. The function returns a tuple of the six global records. For instance, passing an empty input yields a tuple of six empty records.

title: Zoo Enclosure Manager

The input months are a list of records, each a tuple of a month string and a sequence of health indicators. During each month, the system allocates a new list of medical alerts and a new dictionary of daily feedings. Health indicators are evaluated to place poor results into the medical alerts list and normal results into the feedings dictionary. Following the month, the medical alerts are appended to the quarantined individuals list and the feedings dictionary updates the diet requirements dictionary. The function returns a tuple of the six main containers. Given an empty list of months, the output is a tuple of six empty trackers.

The weeks input is a list of weekly schedules, each a tuple of a week identifier and a sequence of attendance logs. Item tags are inspected, placing problematic items in the stains list and standard items in the fabric dictionary. title: Botanical Greenhouse Controller

The seasons input is a list of climatic periods, each a tuple of a season name and a sequence of growth measurements. While evaluating each period, the system initializes a fresh list of pest sightings and a fresh dictionary of humidity adjustments. Growth measurements determine if an entry goes to the pest sightings list or the humidity adjustments dictionary. At the end of the period, the pest sightings are added to the diseased plants list and the humidity dictionary updates the soil moistures dictionary. The function returns a tuple of the six trackers.
