Set up separate sequences to track instruments needing basic restringing, violins requiring severe crack repairs, cellos waiting for soundpost adjustments, and completely restored string instruments. You need mappings that relate specific wood types to their resonant frequencies, connect individual musicians to their instrument appraisal values, and associate varnish recipes with their necessary curing times. As the workshop records are evaluated, move any instruments with unfixable structural damage into a permanent salvage list, and collect rare antique bows needing rehairing into a specialized artisan queue. Return a tuple detailing the wood type with the highest frequency, the musician with the most valuable instrument, and the number of completely restored string instruments. Example input: workshop repair tags and material logs. Output: wood type name, musician name, and restored count.

title: Rare Book Bindery Coordinator
spec: Create a function `assemble(volumes)` to analyze the workflow in an artisanal rare book bindery. The logic must track independent sequences for pages waiting for hand sewing, leather covers being stamped, finished leather-bound classics, and delicate vellum manuscripts. Additionally, implement mappings to connect specific thread materials to their tensile strengths, link historical eras to their typical cover motifs, and associate apprentice binders with their weekly error counts. While parsing the daily progress logs, direct any torn pages into a paper mending list, and record requests for gold leaf lettering into a specialized finishing sequence. Return a tuple containing the thread material with the highest tensile strength, the historical era with the most motifs, and the count of delicate vellum manuscripts. Example input: daily bindery tickets and material properties. Output: thread material name, historical era string, and manuscript count.

title: Medieval Blacksmith Forge Coordinator
spec: Implement `process(commissions)` to manage the daily fires of a bustling blacksmith forge. Initialize distinct lists for crude iron nails, hardened steel weapons, decorative wrought iron gates, and specialized farrier horseshoes. You must also create mappings that relate specific coal types to their burn temperatures, connect apprentice smiths to their daily hammer strike counts, and associate noble patrons with their outstanding debts. As the forging commissions are processed, divert any warped steel items into a remelting scrap heap sequence, and log perfectly balanced blades into a royal armory presentation list. Return a tuple identifying the coal type burning the hottest, the patron with the largest debt, and the total number of hardened steel weapons. Example input: patron orders and forge temperature readings. Output: coal type string, patron name, and weapon count.

title: Software Patch Dependency Grapher
spec: You are writing a tool to determine the order of software updates. The entry function is `resolve(patches)`. The input is a list of tuples providing a patch name, a list of required prior patches, and a status string. The logic must track forward dependencies, reverse dependencies, and root patches to build the graph structure. It also needs to categorize the provided patches into separate collections for installed items, missing items, and conflicted items. During the graph traversal, maintain a processing queue and a sequence for the final installation order. Return a tuple containing the final installation order and the conflicted items. For example, providing three patches with one unmet requirement will yield a sequence of two and one conflict.

title: Renaissance Fresco Pigment Restorer
spec: You are developing a tool for art historians to analyze damaged murals. The entry function is `restore(flakes)`. The input is a list of tuples detailing a section coordinate, a color hue, and a degradation level. The categorization step must sort the samples into ultramarine blues, ochre yellows, and cinnabar reds. The mapping step tracks the artwork condition by associating sections with moisture damage, soot accumulation, and plaster cracks. The restoration step evaluates the data to compile pristine preserved areas and sections requiring immediate intervention. Return a tuple of the pristine preserved areas and the moisture damage records. For example, evaluating five flakes might return two pristine areas and one moisture record.

title: Astronomical Star Catalog Matcher
spec: You are writing a program to reconcile astronomical databases. The entry function is `crossmatch(stars)`. The input is a list of tuples containing a star identifier, right ascension, declination, and classification. The parsing stage must separate the records into a collection for catalog one and a collection for catalog two. The grouping stage must classify the stars by maintaining mappings for binary systems, variable stars, and high proper motion stars. The matching stage evaluates coordinate distances and must track successfully matched pairs, unmatched orphans, and data anomalies. Return a tuple of the matched pairs and the unmatched orphans. For example, comparing five stars might yield two matched pairs and one orphan.

title: Medieval Castle Siege Simulator
spec: You are designing the backend for a historical warfare simulation. The entry function is `defend(events)`. The input is a list of tuples describing an attack sector and the siege weapon used. The setup phase must establish the current state by tracking wall damage levels, garrison strengths, and active fire locations. The processing phase evaluates each attack and must collect breached sectors, fallen defenders, and depleted armories. The final assessment tracks the surviving units and captured siege engines. Return a tuple of the surviving units and the breached sectors. For example, processing five attacks on three sectors might return a dozen surviving units and one breached sector.

title: Geological Core Sample Analyzer
spec: You are building a pipeline to process drilling data. The entry function is `analyze(layers)`. The input is a list of strings detailing depth, rock type, and field notes. The parsing step must sort the layers into igneous rocks, sedimentary rocks, and metamorphic rocks. The tracking step evaluates the notes to map out fossil locations, oil deposits, and underground water reservoirs. The analysis phase must collect anomalous depths that violate standard geological ordering and build an overall profile summary sequence. Return a tuple of the profile summary sequence and the fossil locations. For example, inputting four layers might return a sequence of four rock profiles and one fossil coordinate.

title: Semiconductor Wafer Defect Analyzer
spec: You are creating quality control software for microchip manufacturing. The entry function is `inspect(wafers)`. The input is a list of tuples containing a wafer identifier, a defect coordinate, and a particle size. The categorization step must classify the flaws into surface scratches, structural microcracks, and chemical impurities. The mapping step tracks factory conditions by associating wafers with machine calibrations, cleanroom temperatures, and exposure times. The quality control step must compile approved production batches and rejected scrap materials. Return a tuple of the approved production batches and the surface scratches. For example, inspecting six wafers might return four approved batches and two scratches.

title: Boreal Forest Wildfire Tracker
spec: You are developing a response coordination system for natural disasters. The entry function is `track(reports)`. The input is a list of tuples detailing a forest sector, a temperature, and a wind speed. The categorization phase must divide the sectors into active fronts, contained zones, and extinguished areas. The mapping phase tracks hazards by associating sectors with hot spots, smoke plumes, and safe evacuation routes. The logistics phase coordinates the response by collecting deployed ground crews and requested aerial water drops. Return a tuple of the active fronts and the evacuation routes. For example, processing four sector reports might yield two active fronts and one primary evacuation route.

title: Cybernetic Prosthetic Neural Calibrator
spec: You are programming the signal processing logic for a bionic limb. The entry function is `calibrate(signals)`. The input is a list of tuples containing an electrode identifier, a voltage, and a muscle group. The sorting stage must divide the electrical impulses into motor commands, sensory feedback, and resting tremors. The mapping stage tracks the nervous system by associating electrodes with motor cortex synapses, peripheral nerve endings, and signal latencies. The calibration stage must compile optimized movement patterns and rejected interference spikes. Return a tuple of the optimized movement patterns and the sensory feedback. For example, evaluating ten signals might return two movement patterns and three feedback responses.

title: Quantum Circuit Gate Optimizer
spec: You are building a compiler pass for quantum computing hardware. The entry function is `optimize(gates)`. The input is a list of strings detailing a quantum gate type and a target qubit. The parsing step must categorize the instructions into single qubit gates, multi qubit gates, and measurement operations. The mapping step tracks the quantum state by associating qubits with entangled pairs, phase shifts, and error rates. The optimization pass must collect redundant gates marked for removal and build the final optimized execution sequence. Return a tuple of the optimized execution sequence and the entangled pairs. For example, passing six gates with a cancellation might return an optimized sequence of four gates and one pair.

title: Choreography Dance Step Sequencer
spec: You are designing software to help directors visualize stage performances. The entry function is `sequence(moves)`. The input is a list of tuples containing a dancer identifier, a stage position, and a musical beat. The setup phase must divide the routines into solo moves, partner lifts, and group formations. The mapping phase tracks the stage environment by associating beats with stage positions, costume changes, and prop usage. The timeline phase evaluates trajectories to collect potential dancer collisions and compile the final performance timeline. Return a tuple of the performance timeline and the collisions. For example, evaluating five moves might yield a sequence of five steps and zero collisions.

title: Subatomic Particle Collision Tracker
spec: You are writing a data analysis tool for a particle accelerator. The entry function is `monitor(collisions)`. The input is a list of tuples containing an event identifier, an energy level, and a trajectory angle. The filtering step must categorize the particles into alpha particles, beta particles, and gamma rays. The mapping step tracks the physics by associating events with quantum tunneling, magnetic deflections, and decay rates. The reporting step must compile confirmed discoveries and background noise events. Return a tuple of the confirmed discoveries and the alpha particles. For example, processing five collisions might return one discovery and two alpha particles.

title: Tectonic Plate Fault Line Mapper
spec: You are developing a seismological analysis program. The entry function is `map(tremors)`. The input is a list of tuples detailing a fault region, a magnitude, and a depth. The sorting step must separate the events into convergent boundaries, divergent boundaries, and transform faults. The mapping step tracks geological shifts by associating regions with crustal stress, magma chamber pressures, and tsunami risks. The analysis step must compile high risk earthquake zones and stable continental shields. Return a tuple of the high risk earthquake zones and the convergent boundaries. For example, mapping eight tremors might return two high risk zones and three convergent boundaries.

title: Satellite Downlink Scheduler
spec: You are building an orbital communications coordinator. The entry function is `schedule(requests)`. The input is a list of tuples detailing a satellite identifier, a data volume, and a priority level. The queuing step must divide the transmissions into high priority requests, medium priority requests, and low priority requests. The mapping step tracks infrastructure by associating satellites with ground stations, bandwidth usage, and local weather delays. The logistics step evaluates the schedule to collect successful downlinks and missed orbital passes. Return a tuple of the successful downlinks and the missed passes. For example, evaluating four transmission requests might yield three successful downlinks and one missed pass.

title: Synthetic Biology Plasmid Constructor
spec: You are writing software to automate genetic engineering designs. The entry function is `construct(sequences)`. The input is a list of tuples containing a sequence identifier, a nucleotide string, and a genetic feature type. The extraction step must categorize the genetic parts into promoters, coding sequences, and terminators. The mapping step tracks the biological properties by associating sequences with restriction sites, antibiotic resistance genes, and origins of replication. The assembly step combines compatible parts and must collect valid plasmids and unstable biological constructs. Return a tuple of the valid plasmids and the unstable constructs. For example, passing five genetic parts might return one valid plasmid and one unstable sequence.

title: Atmospheric Greenhouse Gas Profiler
spec: You are creating a tool to analyze meteorological balloon data. The entry function is `profile(samples)`. The input is a list of tuples detailing an altitude, a gas concentration, and a temperature. The categorization step must sort the readings into carbon dioxide layers, methane pockets, and nitrous oxide traces. The mapping step tracks the climate by associating altitudes with ozone depletion, thermal inversions, and solar radiation absorption. The forecast step must compile severe warming zones and stable atmospheric layers. Return a tuple of the severe warming zones and the methane pockets. For example, profiling six samples might return two severe zones and one methane pocket.

title: Cartographic Map Projection Converter
spec: You are developing a geographic information processing tool. The entry function is `convert(coordinates)`. The input is a list of tuples containing a latitude, a longitude, and an elevation. The filtering step must sort the geographic coordinates into northern hemisphere points, southern hemisphere points, and equatorial points. The mapping step evaluates mathematical bounds to associate coordinates with polar distortions, valid mercator regions, and robinson interpolations. The output step must compile successfully projected map points and out of bounds projection errors. Return a tuple of the successfully projected points and the out of bounds errors. For example, converting three points might return two projected points and one error.

title: Folklore Mythological Motif Indexer
spec: You are building an academic database tool for literary anthropologists. The entry function is `index(tales)`. The input is a list of tuples containing a story title, an origin region, and a main literary theme. The sorting step must categorize the stories into creation myths, trickster tales, and heroic epics. The mapping step tracks cultural elements by associating regions with animal spirits, pantheon deities, and underworld journeys. The cross reference step must compile shared motifs across different regions and unique local legends. Return a tuple of the shared motifs and the creation myths. For example, indexing four stories might yield one shared motif and two creation myths.

title: Deep Sea Hydrothermal Vent Explorer
spec: You are programming a navigation and analysis system for an autonomous submarine. The entry function is `explore(vents)`. The input is a list of tuples detailing a vent identifier, a temperature, and a depth. The categorization step must sort the formations into black smokers, white smokers, and cold seeps. The mapping step tracks the ecology by associating vents with tubeworm colonies, extremophile bacteria, and mineral deposits. The charting step must compile safe submersible routes and hazardous pressure zones. Return a tuple of the safe submersible routes and the black smokers. For example, analyzing four vents might return two safe routes and one black smoker.

title: Epidemic Contact Tracing Graph
spec: You are writing a public health analysis tool. The entry function is `trace(contacts)`. The input is a list of tuples containing an individual identifier, an exposed person identifier, and an exposure duration. The node step must categorize the population into patient zeros, primary contacts, and secondary contacts. The mapping step tracks the transmission by associating individuals with exposure clusters, mandatory quarantine statuses, and medical test results. The output step must compile high risk individuals requiring immediate testing and cleared individuals. Return a tuple of the high risk individuals and the exposure clusters. For example, tracing five interactions might return three high risk individuals and one cluster.

title: Linguistic Dialect Syntax Comparator
spec: You are developing a computational linguistics analyzer. The entry function is `compare(sentences)`. The input is a list of tuples detailing a region, a grammatical structure, and a vocabulary word. The parsing step must sort the speech patterns into subject verb object structures, subject object verb structures, and anomalous structures. The mapping step tracks linguistic evolution by associating regions with local slang, phonetic shifts, and adopted loan words. The analysis step must compile shared syntax rules across regions and diverging grammar patterns. Return a tuple of the shared syntax rules and the anomalous structures. For example, analyzing four sentences might yield two shared rules and one anomaly.

title: Entomological Butterfly Migration Tracker
spec: You are creating a biodiversity monitoring system. The entry function is `follow(sightings)`. The input is a list of tuples containing a species name, a geographical location, and a wing condition rating. The grouping step must categorize the insects into monarchs, swallowtails, and painted ladies. The mapping step tracks the journey by associating locations with resting grounds, nectar food sources, and predator activities. The routing step evaluates the data to compile primary migration paths and straggler insects left behind. Return a tuple of the primary migration paths and the stragglers. For example, processing five sightings might return two migration paths and one straggler.

title: Hydropower Dam Spillway Controller
spec: You are programming the safety logic for a hydroelectric facility. The entry function is `control(sensors)`. The input is a list of tuples detailing a reservoir section, a water level metric, and a flow rate. The zone step must classify the water volumes into critical levels, nominal levels, and low levels. The mapping step tracks the dam infrastructure by associating sections with open spillways, active turbine speeds, and dangerous silt buildup. The action step must compile automated water releases and manual system overrides. Return a tuple of the automated releases and the critical levels. For example, monitoring four sections might return one automated release and one critical level.

title: Urban Rooftop Garden Pollinator Tracker
spec: You are writing a tool to study urban ecology. The entry function is `observe(visits)`. The input is a list of tuples containing a building name, an insect classification, and a plant visited. The insect step must sort the visitors into honeybees, bumblebees, and solitary bees. The mapping step tracks the urban ecosystem by associating buildings with flowering plants, nesting sites, and pesticide risks. The route step evaluates the visits to compile active pollinator corridors and isolated gardens lacking visits. Return a tuple of the pollinator corridors and the solitary bees. For example, tracking six visits might return two pollinator corridors and one solitary bee.

title: Deep Space Telescope Signal Filter
spec: You are developing the initial processing pipeline for an astronomical observatory. The entry function is `filter(signals)`. The input is a list of tuples detailing a frequency, a signal intensity, and a duration. The band step must categorize the captures into radio waves, microwaves, and infrared signals. The mapping step tracks the cosmos by associating frequencies with known pulsars, solar flares, and cosmic background noise. The detection step must compile unexplained anomalies and identified human satellites. Return a tuple of the unexplained anomalies and the radio waves. For example, processing four signals might yield one anomaly and two radio waves.

title: Volcanic Ash Plume Dispersion Modeler
spec: You are creating a hazard forecasting tool for aviation safety. The entry function is `model(eruptions)`. The input is a list of tuples containing a volcano name, an ash column height, and a wind direction. The altitude step must divide the airborne particles into low atmospheric ash, stratospheric ash, and tropospheric ash. The mapping step tracks the hazard by associating regions with grounded flights, air quality warnings, and ashfall deposits. The forecast step must compile safe air corridors and hazardous flight zones. Return a tuple of the safe air corridors and the grounded flights. For example, modeling three eruptions might yield two safe corridors and one grounded region.

title: Spacefleet Mission Control
spec: `monitor(telemetry)` processes spaceship signals provided as tuples of ship name, sector, status, and class. The system must initialize separate empty lists for active ships, destroyed ships, ships needing repair, and unknown signals. It must also prepare empty dictionaries to group ships by their sector and to group them by their class, alongside an empty list for tracking error messages. As it iterates through the telemetry, it populates these structures, creating a new empty list for any newly encountered sector or class before appending the ship. Finally, it constructs a summary dictionary containing these categorized lists and returns a tuple of the summary dictionary and the error messages list. For example, given an input with a single tuple containing apollo, alpha, active, explorer, it returns a tuple where the first element is the summary dictionary containing apollo in the active list and in the alpha sector dictionary, and the second element is an empty error list.

title: Wildlife Safari Tracker
spec: `track(sightings)` analyzes animal observations given as tuples of animal species, zone, health status, and age group. The logic requires initializing distinct empty lists for healthy animals, injured animals, missing animals, and anomalous records. It also requires setting up empty dictionaries to group animals by their observation zone and to group them by their species, plus an empty list to hold alert notifications. When processing each observation, if the zone or species is seen for the first time, the logic must initialize a new empty list for it before adding the animal. The function builds an overarching summary dictionary containing all these associations and lists, then returns a tuple of the summary dictionary and the alert notifications list. For example, if provided a list with a tuple of lion, north zone, healthy, and adult, it returns a summary dictionary with the north zone containing the lion and the healthy list holding the lion, alongside an empty alert list.

title: Food Truck Network
spec: `manage(transactions)` evaluates food truck sales data provided as tuples of truck identifier, neighborhood, item sold, and profit margin. The function must start by creating empty lists for highly profitable sales, average sales, loss making sales, and unclassified transactions. It also initializes empty dictionaries to track sales by neighborhood and sales by truck identifier, along with an empty list for compliance warnings. For each transaction, if a neighborhood or truck identifier has not been encountered, the logic must assign a new empty list to that key before recording the sale. Afterward, it packages these categorizations into a fresh summary dictionary and returns a tuple of this summary and the warnings list. For example, an input list with a tuple of taco truck, downtown, tacos, and high profit will yield a summary dictionary holding taco truck in the highly profitable list and downtown dictionary, returned alongside an empty warnings list.

title: High School Tournament
spec: `evaluate(matches)` calculates sports tournament results from inputs containing school name, division, match outcome, and sport type. The algorithm first initializes separate empty lists for schools that won, schools that tied, schools that lost, and disqualified entries. It prepares empty dictionaries to organize results by division and by sport type, as well as an empty list for referee complaints. During the evaluation of matches, encountering a new division or a new sport type requires initializing a new empty list for it before storing the school name. The function gathers all these results into an empty summary dictionary and returns a tuple of the summary and the complaints list. For example, providing a list with a tuple of tigers, division one, won, and basketball results in a summary dictionary where division one and the won list both contain tigers, accompanied by an empty complaints list.

title: Hospital Triage Center
spec: `triage(patients)` organizes emergency room arrivals given as tuples of patient name, ward, severity level, and symptom category. The process begins by creating empty lists for critical patients, stable patients, discharged patients, and unassigned cases. It sets up empty dictionaries to categorize patients by their assigned ward and by their symptom category, along with an empty list for medical supply requests. As it processes arrivals, any newly seen ward or symptom category must first be initialized with an empty list before adding the patient. The function compiles the organized data into a new summary dictionary and returns a tuple of the summary and the medical supply requests list. For example, given an input list with a tuple of john doe, icu, critical, and cardiac, it returns a summary dictionary holding john doe in the critical list and icu dictionary, along with an empty medical supply requests list.

title: Ebook Library Organizer
spec: `organize(books)` sorts digital books provided as tuples of title, genre, author, and reading status. The logic mandates setting up an empty dictionary for genre classifications and another empty dictionary for author portfolios. It also requires creating empty lists to track completed books, currently reading books, and unread books. The function must iterate through the provided books. When a genre or an author is missing from their respective dictionary, the code must create a new empty list for them. Additionally, it maintains an empty list for corrupted files encountered during processing. After sorting everything, it creates an empty metadata dictionary, populates it with the totals, and returns a tuple of the author portfolios and the reading status lists. For example, an input list with a tuple of dune, sci-fi, herbert, and completed yields a tuple containing the author portfolios dictionary with herbert holding dune, and the reading status lists where the completed list contains dune.

title: Smart City Traffic Control
spec: `route(vehicles)` directs smart cars using tuples containing license plate, destination zone, vehicle type, and battery level. The main logic initializes an empty dictionary to hold traffic queues for each destination zone and an empty dictionary for vehicle types. It creates separate empty lists for fully charged vehicles, low battery vehicles, and critically low vehicles. A dedicated helper function should be used to parse individual vehicle alerts, which itself initializes an empty list for local warnings and an empty dictionary for route suggestions. Whenever the main loop finds a new destination or vehicle type, it must initialize an empty list there. The entry function returns a tuple of the destination traffic queues and the battery level lists. For example, if the input contains a tuple of plate one, downtown, sedan, and fully charged, it returns a tuple with the destination queues dictionary mapping downtown to plate one, and the battery lists where the fully charged list contains plate one.

title: Online Multiplayer Matchmaker
spec: `match(players)` pairs gamers based on inputs containing username, server region, skill tier, and connection latency. The matchmaking system starts by creating empty dictionaries for server regions and skill tiers. It needs separate empty lists for players with excellent connections, moderate connections, and poor connections. A helper routine is responsible for forming the actual squads, which initializes an empty list for valid squads and an empty list for isolated players. When categorizing players in the main routine, any unrecorded server region or skill tier must be initialized with an empty list before the username is appended. The function returns a tuple of the valid squads list and the regional dictionaries. For example, given a tuple of sniper ghost, north america, gold tier, and excellent connection, it returns a tuple with the valid squads list containing the player, and the regional dictionaries associating north america with sniper ghost.

title: Grocery Supply Chain
spec: `distribute(shipments)` allocates produce using tuples of item name, warehouse location, perishability, and supplier name. The system sets up empty dictionaries to track inventory per warehouse and inventory per supplier. It creates distinct empty lists for highly perishable items, stable items, and expired items. While processing the shipments, discovering a new warehouse or a new supplier requires the logic to associate them with a new empty list before adding the item. A supplementary function calculates supply gaps, initializing an empty list for missing items and an empty dictionary for reorder quantities. The main function returns a tuple of the warehouse dictionary and the missing items list. For example, an input with a tuple of apples, north warehouse, highly perishable, and local farms yields a tuple containing the warehouse dictionary associating north warehouse with apples, and an empty missing items list.

title: Cyber Defense Sentinel
spec: `defend(threats)` analyzes network anomalies presented as tuples of ip address, attack vector, severity, and target protocol. The defensive algorithm initializes empty dictionaries to group threats by attack vector and by target protocol. It requires independent empty lists for blocked threats, monitored threats, and ignored threats. While evaluating the anomalies, if an attack vector or protocol is not yet tracked, it must be assigned a new empty list prior to adding the ip address. A logging helper function processes the aftermath, initializing an empty list for forensic logs and an empty dictionary for quarantine zones. The entry function returns a tuple of the blocked threats list and the protocol dictionary. For example, providing a tuple of local host, malware, severe, and http results in a tuple containing the blocked threats list with local host, and the protocol dictionary associating http with local host.

title: Real Estate Portfolio
spec: `assess(properties)` evaluates building assets given as tuples of address, city, condition rating, and property type. The evaluation starts by establishing empty dictionaries to cluster properties by city and by property type. It mandates distinct empty lists for newly renovated properties, properties needing minor fixes, and properties requiring major overhauls. Whenever a new city or property type is encountered in the iteration, a new empty list must be created for it. An external valuation helper function computes market values, initializing an empty list for premium listings and an empty dictionary for tax liabilities. The main routine returns a tuple of the city clusters dictionary and the premium listings list. For example, an input tuple of main street, springfield, newly renovated, and commercial yields a tuple with the city clusters dictionary mapping springfield to main street, and an empty premium listings list.

title: Galactic Trade Network
spec: `trade(cargo)` manages interstellar shipments provided as tuples of commodity, destination planet, legality, and merchant guild. The trading hub initializes empty dictionaries to organize cargo by destination planet and by merchant guild. It requires separate empty lists for legal goods, contraband, and restricted items. During the sorting process, any destination planet or merchant guild seen for the first time must be paired with a new empty list before the commodity is added. A customs helper function checks cargo clearance, creating an empty list for seized goods and an empty dictionary for fined merchants. The function returns a tuple of the destination cargo dictionary and the seized goods list. For example, given a tuple of spices, mars, legal, and trade guild, the function returns a tuple containing the destination cargo dictionary mapping mars to spices, and an empty seized goods list.

title: Vintage Arcade Emulator
spec: `emulate(roms)` categorizes game files supplied as tuples of game title, console system, genre, and compatibility status. The emulation manager prepares empty dictionaries to sort games by console system and by genre. It relies on separate empty lists for perfectly compatible games, playable games with glitches, and unplayable games. As it iterates through the game files, any unencountered console system or genre must be initialized with an empty list before appending the game title. A configuration helper applies user settings, initializing an empty list for custom keybinds and an empty dictionary for video filters. The entry function returns a tuple of the genre sorting dictionary and the unplayable games list. For example, providing a tuple of pacman, arcade, maze, and perfectly compatible returns a tuple containing the genre sorting dictionary mapping maze to pacman, and an empty unplayable games list.

title: Automated Factory Assembly
spec: `assemble(components)` routes mechanical parts provided as tuples of part serial, workstation, material type, and quality check result. The routing logic establishes empty dictionaries to group parts by workstation and by material type. It utilizes individual empty lists for parts that passed inspection, parts needing rework, and scrapped parts. While scanning the components, discovering a new workstation or a new material type dictates creating a new empty list for that category. A secondary packaging function prepares the final products, initializing an empty list for boxed items and an empty dictionary for shipping labels. The system returns a tuple of the workstation dictionary and the scrapped parts list. For example, an input tuple of gear one, welding, steel, and passed returns a tuple with the workstation dictionary associating welding with gear one, and an empty scrapped parts list.

title: Music Festival Lineup
spec: `schedule(bands)` organizes performances based on tuples of band name, stage name, music genre, and crowd capacity. The scheduling engine initializes empty dictionaries to allocate bands per stage and per music genre. It needs separate empty lists for headline acts, supporting acts, and local openers. When processing the performances, an unrecorded stage or genre requires the initialization of a new empty list. A ticketing helper function calculates expected attendance, setting up an empty list for sold out shows and an empty dictionary for VIP guest lists. The function returns a tuple of the stage allocations dictionary and the headline acts list. For example, given a tuple of rock band, main stage, rock, and headline act, it returns a tuple containing the stage allocations dictionary mapping main stage to rock band, and the headline acts list containing rock band.

title: Cloud Server Provisioning
spec: `provision(requests)` handles infrastructure demands given as tuples of instance name, data center, operating system, and resource tier. The cloud controller sets up empty dictionaries to track instances by data center and by operating system. It initiates distinct empty lists for high performance instances, standard instances, and budget instances. During request handling, any newly observed data center or operating system must be mapped to a new empty list. A billing helper function estimates monthly costs, which initializes an empty list for discounted accounts and an empty dictionary for usage limits. The main function returns a tuple of the data center tracking dictionary and the budget instances list. For example, providing a tuple of server alpha, east region, linux, and high performance yields a tuple containing the data center tracking dictionary mapping east region to server alpha, and an empty budget instances list.

title: Cinema Ticketing Kiosk
spec: `issue(tickets)` processes movie admissions using tuples of customer name, movie title, showtime, and ticket category. The kiosk system creates empty dictionaries to aggregate customers by movie title and by showtime. It maintains individual empty lists for adult tickets, child tickets, and senior citizen tickets. While iterating through the admissions, if a movie title or showtime is new, it must be initialized with an empty list. A concession helper function processes food orders, initiating an empty list for combo meals and an empty dictionary for beverage choices. The entry function returns a tuple of the showtime aggregations dictionary and the child tickets list. For example, an input tuple of alice, star wars, evening, and adult returns a tuple containing the showtime aggregations dictionary mapping evening to alice, and an empty child tickets list.

title: Oceanographic Sensor Buoys
spec: `measure(readings)` collates marine data provided as tuples of sensor identifier, ocean region, measurement type, and equipment status. The data processor initiates empty dictionaries to group sensors by ocean region and by measurement type.
